Aisha (runtime): Heads-up — canary node group saw repeated OOMs on v2.3.4 canary runs. Not classic leak: RSS creeps up over ~20m requests then spikes and we hit OOM killer. Suspect page fragmentation / un-coalesced anon pages after compaction. Anyone able to run quick sampling on a repro workload?

Ben R.: Can you paste the pmap/smaps snapshot and the job id? I can run a few memmap diffs.

Aisha (runtime): Job: canary-ec2-g4dn-2026-03-15-17, PID on failing container was 4872. Attached small snippet from last crash: `OOM killed process 4872 (redwood-worker) total-vm:124832000kB, anon-rss:91840000kB`

Charlie M.: Interesting — anon-rss high. Two quick things to collect: `cat /proc/4872/smaps > /tmp/smaps.4872.before` and `jeprof`/malloc stats if using jemalloc. Also check `grep -i huge /proc/4872/numa_maps` and `sysctl vm.nr_hugepages` to see if THP is toggling.

Aisha (runtime): We're on glibc + tcmalloc on that image (not jemalloc). Will grab smaps. Also the runtime uses a user-space page-coalescer we added last quarter; maybe it's not firing for short-lived buffers.

Dana S. (perf): If tcmalloc, please run `pprof` or `heap-profile` from runtime (`/debug/heapz`) — but the quickest is a sampled anonymous page map over time. I have a tiny script I use:

```
#!/bin/bash
PID=$1
for i in {1..6}; do
  echo "--- $(date) ---" >> /tmp/pagemap.$PID.log
  awk '/AnonHugePages|Rss|VmSwap|VmSize/ {print}' /proc/$PID/status >> /tmp/pagemap.$PID.log
  cat /proc/$PID/smaps | awk '/^Rss:|^AnonHugePages:|^Size:|^KernelPageSize:/' >> /tmp/pagemap.$PID.log
  sleep 10
done
```

Dana S. (perf): Drop that and send logs — look for many small `Size:` lines adding up but no contiguous ranges (that's fragmentation).

Ben R.: Also try `numactl --hardware` and `numastat -p 4872` on the host. If pages are scattered across nodes it costs compaction. I can run a quick synthetic that allocates lots of short-lived 4k buffers to see if page merging fails.

Aisha (runtime): Running script now on canary host; logs to `/tmp/pagemap.4872.log`. FYI runtime is doing a lot of mmap/madvise(MADV_DONTNEED) cycles during generation — maybe we are leaving pages in the kernel free but not coalesced.

ci-bot: perf/run/1793123456 completed — flamegraph and allocator trace uploaded: https://internal.ci/redwood/perf/1793123456 (flamegraph + raw profiles) :rocket:

Charlie M.: Nice. I pulled the flamegraph — most time in tokenizer and small object churn. For memory, can you `echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory` on the host (careful on prod) and see whether RSS drops? That triggers kernel compaction to attempt to coalesce free pages.

Aisha (runtime): Ran compact_memory on canary host — small immediate drop (~30MB) but pattern repeats and OOM still after ~18m. I captured `smaps` diffs and attached first 3 dumps below (trimmed):
- `Size:   4096 kB` repeated 2000x across different anon mappings
- `Rss:    16 kB` for many, but total accumulative large
- no large contiguous `Size:` ranges seen

Dana S. (perf): That aligns with fragmentation. Next experiment: try enabling hugepage coalescing at runtime and/or batching allocations so many small buffers are freed together. In the codebase, there's a flag `--batch-kv-free` (runtime flags) — toggling to true delays frees and does them in one loop; could reduce fragmentation. Can you try a canary with `--batch-kv-free` enabled?

Ben R.: Also try building tcmalloc with page coalescing patches? But quicker: run the synthetic small-buffer alloc test I mentioned and compare `pagemap` with/without `--batch-kv-free`. I'll stand up the test tomorrow morning.

Aisha (runtime): I'll spin a canary variant with `--batch-kv-free` and collect smaps+numastat. ETA ~2h. If that reduces fragmentation we push a temp mitigation until we upstream a smarter allocator fix.

Charlie M.: If `--batch-kv-free` helps, we should add a metric `allocator.fragmentation_ratio` and alert if it exceeds threshold. Also add a periodic `smaps-sampler` job in our perf harness.

Aisha (runtime): Agreed. I'll post the logs here when ready. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Ben R.: Ping me once logs are up, I'll run the synthetic and compare. :eyes:

Dana S. (perf): If you want, I can do an async PR to add the sampler + Grafana dashboard once you confirm.

Aisha (runtime): Thanks — will follow up with dumps and canary id. End of thread for now.
